comps: Korn Ferry and Heidrick & Struggles (retained search, about a third of first-year compensation)
Robert Half's permanent placement segment ($440m in 2025, a percentage of annual compensation)
cards.excl: Excludes $140bn of temporary help, which bills an hourly markup — 73% of the code's payroll.
cards.invoice: a percentage of the placed candidate's first-year salary
kill: Retained or contingency? Both are priced as a share of salary; they differ in who carries a failed search. Retained firms are paid in instalments whatever the outcome — safer revenue.
What share of placements come from one client? Concentration is where the fee gets renegotiated.
Does the ATS belong to the client or to you? If theirs, they own the candidate graph.
cards.name: Executive search & permanent placement

roles.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel

cards.stance_why: The fee is a share of the placed candidate's salary. The client never sees your cost base, so a cheaper process does not give them anything to negotiate against.
cards.why: The fee is indexed to someone else's wage bill, so the client cannot see your cost base and has nothing to index a discount to. Sourcing, screening and scheduling are the cost; the placement fee is unchanged by how they get done.

comps: Doma (bought by Title Resources Group, Sept 2024)
cards.excl: No industry code isolates title and escrow — BLS files it inside legal services and insurance carriers. Payroll here is the one occupation that exists only for this work (title examiners, abstractors and searchers), so it understates the business: closers and escrow officers are filed under general clerical codes.
cards.invoice: a premium scaled to the policy amount, at a state-set or filed rate
kill: A regulator that sets the rate can cut it: Texas cut its promulgated title rates 10% from July 2025.

Agent or underwriter? On agent-written policies the agent keeps most of the premium — about 83% at Stewart in Q3 2025 — and the underwriter's share is contractual. Which side of that split a business sits on decides what it keeps.

Fannie Mae's title acceptance pilot drops title insurance entirely on some low loan-to-value refinances, and FHFA said in June 2026 it is expanding. If it reaches purchase loans, the premium itself is at risk.
What share of revenue is premium versus escrow and closing fees? Only the premium is tied to a set or filed rate — check how the rest is priced.
cards.name: Title insurance, escrow & settlement
cards.stance_why: The premium scales with the price of the property, at a rate the state sets outright (Texas, New Mexico, Florida) or that must be filed with it. It is priced off the policy amount, not off what a given search costs, so a cheaper search gives the buyer nothing to bargain against — though a state that sets the rate can pass industry-wide savings through at its next rate hearing.
cards.why: The search and examination are the cost: pulling and reading the chain of recorded documents. Counties covering over 90% of the US population now accept electronic recording, so the inputs are increasingly digital while the premium stays tied to the price of the house.

cards.invoice: a fixed fee per test, set by the payer
kill: What share of revenue is Medicare/Medicaid? Schedule cuts are the real risk, not competition.
Is the LIS integrated with the referring EHR? Epic in the middle is a gatekeeper on your data.
Does any test require a pathologist signature by statute? That caps throughput per licence.
cards.name: Diagnostic & medical laboratories

roles.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel

cards.stance_why: Price is set by the payer's reimbursement schedule, not by your cost. It holds until the schedule is next reset — and schedule cuts are the real risk, not competition.
cards.why: Price is set by a reimbursement schedule, not by cost. Accessioning, result entry and billing are labour; the schedule does not move when they get cheaper.

cards.excl: Excludes $82bn of insurance agencies and brokerages, a different business — 72% of the code's payroll.
cards.invoice: a fee per claim or per covered life
kill: Does the carrier re-bid on a cycle? Sophisticated counterparties reprice every 2-3 years.
Who owns the claims history — you or the carrier? It is the only ground truth in a long-horizon domain.
Is any pricing per-FTE? That converts every efficiency gain into a revenue cut.
cards.name: Claims administration & TPA

roles.title: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks

cards.stance_why: Priced per claim or per covered life, which hides the cost base — but carriers are sophisticated buyers who re-bid on a cycle and will reprice at renewal.
cards.why: Per-claim pricing with a long tail before anyone knows the claim was handled well. The verification horizon that makes the work hard to automate is the same thing that stops a cheaper competitor proving they are as good.

comps: Navan (90% transaction revenue, 7% take rate on bookings)
cards.invoice: a commission or transaction fee on the booking value
kill: Is the contract moving to a per-trip SaaS fee? That is the commoditised version.
How much revenue is supplier commission rather than client fee? Suppliers set commissions and can cut them — airlines did in the 2000s.
Self-booking share — already-automated volume is already repriced.
cards.name: Managed travel & booking

roles.title: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel

cards.stance_why: The fee is a share of a booking the client already pays for. Servicing cost is invisible to them; the take rate is conventional.
cards.why: Fee is a percentage of a notional the client is already paying. Servicing cost falls; the take rate is conventional.

cards.invoice: retainer or a percentage of media spend
kill: Is the master services agreement priced on an FTE plan? Then automation cuts revenue 1:1.
What share is production versus strategy? Production is the part that flips.
Client tenure and notice periods — agency books churn faster than the model assumes.
cards.name: Advertising & marketing services

roles.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists

cards.stance_why: A share of media spend is indexed to the client's budget and keeps the saving. A retainer priced off a staffing plan is indexed to your headcount and passes it on. The contract decides which.
cards.why: Where the fee is a share of media spend it is indexed to the client's budget, not to your headcount. Where it is a retainer priced off an FTE plan, it is not — check which.

cards.invoice: a percentage of construction value, or billable hours
kill: What share of the book is percentage-of-value versus time-and-materials?
Does a P.E. stamp gate the deliverable, and can one engineer stamp 10x the volume? If yes the licence is a moat; if liability attaches to the review, it is a ceiling.
Public-sector clients often mandate rate-card disclosure. That kills retention.
cards.name: Engineering & architectural services
cards.scope: Range spans architectural services and engineering services.
cards.stance_why: Percentage-of-construction-value contracts are indexed to the project and keep the saving. Hourly contracts pass it on. The mix inside the firm decides.
cards.why: Percentage-of-construction-value contracts are indexed to the project, not your time. Hourly contracts in the same firm are not. The mix is the whole question.

comps: R1 RCM (taken private by TowerBrook and CD&R, $8.9bn, Nov 2024)
Ensemble Health Partners (Apollo-backed investment at ~$12bn, announced June 2026)
cards.excl: Payroll is medical records specialists (the occupation that includes coders) wherever they work, plus billing and posting clerks inside healthcare. Most of it sits in hospitals and physician offices rather than outsourcers, so this sizes the work, not the outsourced market.
cards.invoice: a percentage of collections when outsourced; a cost centre when in-house
kill: How much of the coding is already done offshore? Where most of it is, the US payroll here overstates what is left to capture.

Payers are automating the other side: UnitedHealth and Cigna face class actions over algorithmic denials, and Medicare began AI-assisted prior authorisation in six states in January 2026. Does faster coding collect more, or just meet faster denials?
Percentage-of-collections contracts keep the saving; per-claim and flat-fee contracts pass it on. What is the mix?
cards.name: Medical coding, billing & revenue-cycle management
cards.stance_why: Vendors quote outsourced revenue-cycle work as a share of what it collects — 4–10% — which would keep the saving. But the payer on the other side is automating too, so part of any gain can go into a faster denial-and-appeal loop rather than into margin.
cards.why: Rule-bound, high-volume and checkable against a fee schedule — the textbook automatable back office. The original plan flagged it as the likely false positive for exactly that reason: the same properties made it some of the first work sent offshore.

kill: Unless engagement letters move to fixed fees, the saving goes to the client.
Attest work needs a licensed signer; the signer-leverage question decides whether the licence is a moat or a ceiling.
Offshore delivery centres already took much of this arbitrage in the 2010s.
cards.name: Accounting & audit practices — the false positive

roles.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel

cards.stance_why: The invoice is denominated in the hours automation removes. Cut the time and you cut the bill — the saving goes to the client unless engagements move to fixed fees first.
cards.why: The most freed payroll of any professional-services archetype here, sitting on an invoice denominated in the hours automation removes. The false positive a naive screen walks into.

not_carded.name: Transfer agency, fund administration & corporate trust
not_carded.why: BLS publishes these only inside all of securities and investments (NAICS 523), where brokers and fund managers dominate the payroll, and no occupation exists only for this work. Any payroll figure would be borrowed from other businesses.

not_carded.name: Credentialing verification
not_carded.why: No industry code of its own and no dedicated occupation — credentialing staff are filed under general records and compliance roles.

not_carded.name: Permit expediting
not_carded.why: Filed under 'all other professional services', with no separate staffing data and no dedicated occupation.

not_carded.name: Retail tax preparation & bookkeeping
not_carded.why: Published inside the same code as the accounting card (NAICS 5412), so their payroll can't be separated from it. Tax preparers alone: $4.3bn of payroll, 39% of their work can go.

not_carded.name: Translation
not_carded.why: Interpreters and translators are a clean anchor — $3.2bn of payroll — but only $0.6bn of their work can go, too little to size an archetype on.

spotcheck.method: 60 payroll-weighted draws with replacement (seed 7) from the tasks the physical gate removed; each judged 'does this mainly need a body?'; 'no' = the gate was wrong. Clopper-Pearson 90% interval.

prose.agreed: The firmest figure is the part all three models agree can go. It sits beside every total on these pages. Where one model never scored a task, there is no three-way figure, and the page says so rather than printing a zero.
caveats: It says what can go under the rule today, not when, how fast, or who keeps the saving. It is not a forecast.
The models disagree a great deal. Lead with the part all three agree on, and read each role's figure as a range.
Gemini ran out of budget before scoring sales, office and administrative work, and part of healthcare, so part of the total was decided by the two Claude models alone.
Whether a business keeps the saving was not measured; every method tried failed a basic noise test.
How hard a task is to specify is not part of the rule; the test that looks at it was designed after seeing the data, so it is exploratory.
Figures on repricing assume a value for how easily one kind of work substitutes for another, so they are modelled, not measured.
No person has judged individual tasks; the check against people is a Labor Department survey of whole jobs.
The public task lists under-describe coordination and exception handling, which pushes the total up.
The filter that removes physical work mislabels a small share of tasks, which pushes the total down.
prose.lede: Which knowledge work AI can take on today, task by task, role by role and industry by industry. Every verdict was judged by AI models, not by people.
prose.rule: A task counts as able to go when three things hold at once: someone can tell within hours whether it was done right, something other than a human expert can check it, and a single mistake is cheap. Work that needs a body is left out. Each task was scored by up to three AI models, and the verdict is their vote.

deals.lede: Two tests, and both must pass: can the work go, and would the owner keep the saving? The census can answer the first. The second it could not measure, so each card's stance is reasoned from how the business prices its work, not measured. Named companies illustrate the pricing model and are not researched targets.
deals.title: What to buy

dial.lede: Every threshold in the rule is a judgement. Each step below loosens one condition, and the total that can go grows as it does. The census uses the middle step.
dial.title: How sure do you want to be?

functions.lede: By business function. The verifier queue is work that is quick to check and cheap to get wrong, but today only a human expert can check it. Whoever builds a reliable automated check for that work turns it into work that can go.
functions.title: What to automate

industries.lede: A task gets the same verdict wherever it is done; industries differ in whom they employ. Each industry's figure is its own staffing times the share of each role's work that can go.
industries.title: Industry by industry

method.lede: Every test the census set itself in advance, reported whether it passed or failed.
method.title: Method, and what failed

roles.lede: Each role's figure is a range, not a rank: tightening or loosening the rule moves it. Open a role to see every task, whether it can go, and why.
roles.title: What happens to a job
